facts.fact: Donald Ross design, opened May 1932; named for Jeremiah Triggs, Providence's parks superintendent; built by the Parks Department's own crews.
Raised greens that slope from back to front; built by Civil Works Administration labour.
The developer chose a Rhode Island Red (2026-10-20).

current.subject: A Rhode Island Red rooster standing in grass.
current.keep: The rooster and its mahogany red.
current.weaknesses: Full body plus grass; the comb and head are small.

concepts.name: Reveille
concepts.rationale: The rooster's head and neck, crowing: tall comb, wattles, mahogany hackles.
concepts.symbolism: Up early for the first tee time.
concepts.tradeoffs: A rooster says Rhode Island more than golf.

concepts.name: Built by Hand
concepts.rationale: A spade driven into a raised green, turf just lifted: the Depression-era crews who built a public course.
references: Built by city crews and CWA labour (fact)
concepts.symbolism: Golf for everyone, made by hand.
concepts.tradeoffs: A spade is a modest image.

recommendation: Concept 1. The crowing rooster is the more memorable mark.
